assessment: Ginger essential oil given intranasally reduced tail-suspension immobility in mice. The elevated plus maze summary reports significant anxiety-like behavior changes for other oils. The study measured no bowel outcome and used no Parkinson cohort.

Cassia and clove essential oils reduced selected inflammatory markers in cells. Table 2 lists no significant tail-suspension or elevated plus maze effect for either. There was no oral spice, Parkinson fatigue, anxiety or constipation comparison.
Intranasal nutmeg essential oil reduced mouse tail-suspension immobility. The experiment used a behavioral proxy, with a different preparation, route and population from the frozen claim.
The essential oil screen measured tail suspension and elevated plus maze behavior after intranasal dosing. Fatigue, constipation and insomnia occur in the background and were unmeasured for nutmeg.
Strawberries appear in prior sensory work cited by the authors. The current experiment measured oral processing of spicy foods and supplied no strawberry exposure or fall outcome.
The food experiment used ground dried chilies and measured oral burn and oral processing. It supplied no Parkinson falls comparison or cayenne-specific clinical effect.

Cumin extract capsules shortened time to first defecation after abdominal surgery in the analyzed sample. This was a short postoperative recovery comparison with extract capsules. The frozen hypothesis specifies ground cumin and Parkinson constipation severity.

Major depression was present before the index overdose. Central nervous system depression in the toxicology discussion refers to reduced neurological activity, without a depression symptom change measurement.
The literature review names parsley in multiplex testing and chervil in family-level allergy background. It supplies no ingredient exposure comparison for Parkinson pain.
The cited mixed sage, mint and oregano case reported angioedema and positive food challenges. It supplies no pain-severity outcome or Parkinson cohort.

The cited toddler case involved anaphylaxis after a marinade containing cayenne and black pepper. The report records rash, eye symptoms, swelling and cough. It supplies no separate pepper comparison or Parkinson pain measure.

These spices occur in a cited curry mixture. Anaphylaxis was attributed to cardamom and fenugreek. Paprika also appears in pediatric sensitization contexts. The reviewed exposures and reactions supply no Parkinson pain comparison.
Eugenol is mentioned among nutmeg compounds. The intervention was nutmeg seed essential oil and the discussion references a prior anxiety proxy. The article supplies no clove anxiety comparison.

Cinnamon and cumin appear as sources of cuminaldehyde. The aging mouse study used the isolated constituent and studied learning and memory. Rigidity appears as disease background rather than as a measured treatment outcome.
Mango is the name of the MRI software. Chronic fatigue syndrome was an exclusion for this cranberry trial, which measured no mango treatment outcome.

Coffee is one of several foods in a high-flavonoid intake exclusion. Caffeine also appears in the background dietary data. The study assigned cranberry powder and did not estimate a coffee effect on fatigue.

The tart cherry concentrate arm reported lower mental fatigue in a healthy middle-aged sample. The study tested concentrate against placebo, with a different form and population from the frozen claim.
Coffee contributed to dietary polyphenols in the study diaries. The study assigned tart cherry concentrate or placebo and supplies no estimate of coffee's effect on fatigue.
